column1: Agent Reliability Scorecard (Agent Backbone Issue #3, Lali Publications)

How to use: fill one row per test question (T01-T20) before you run the agent; paste each reply; score each of the four criteria as a whole number from 1 to 5 using the anchors below. weighted_score and gate fill in automatically in Google Sheets and Excel.
Weighted score = 0.35 x Accuracy + 0.25 x Conciseness + 0.20 x Tone + 0.20 x Actionability (range 1.00 to 5.00). Hard gate: Accuracy of 2 or less is a FAIL whatever the weighted score.

column4: Facts and policy match the source of truth; nothing invented; no claimed action without tool confirmation
column5: Invents a policy, window, exception, discount, feature or completed action, or contradicts the policy doc
column6: Nothing invented, but a detail is wrong in a way that changes what the user does, or a hard rule is softened to maybe
column7: Core policy right; vague or hedged on the edge case; no invented facts
column8: Correct and specific; one minor omission that does not change the user's next action
column9: Exact policy with the specific number or rule; says it does not know or hands off when data is unverified

column4: Answers only the question asked, answer first, in 6 sentences or fewer
column5: 10 or more sentences or about 2x the needed length; answer buried under tangents
column6: About 9 sentences, or the answer comes after a long preamble
column8: 6 sentences or fewer with a little filler, or answer not first
column9: 6 sentences or fewer, answer first, numbered steps for procedures, no filler

column4: Calm, direct, consistent voice, including when the answer is no
column5: Argues, blames the user, hype phrasing, or apology loops
column6: Robotic boilerplate, overly casual, or agrees with a wrong premise to please
column7: Polite and serviceable, but drifts between formal and chatty
column8: Calm and direct with one stray filler phrase
column9: Steady, direct and human; holds a firm no without over-apologizing

column4: Ends with one concrete next step, a confirmed state, or the exact limit and handoff
column5: Ends with a vague offer to help, a dead end, or a false handoff when a path exists
column6: Gives a next step that is wrong or unusable (wrong menu, wrong contact)
column7: Next step when obvious; dead-ends when the request hits a policy limit
column8: Concrete next step missing one detail (for example where to check the result)
column9: Exact UI path, command or confirmed state, or the hard limit plus when to escalate

column2: Slots are a suggestion: T01-T10 your most frequent question types, T11-T15 edge cases, T16-T20 policy traps. Delete unused rows if your set has 15 to 19 questions.
REVIEW (weighted score under 3.00) is an editorial suggestion, not a standard. Set your own bar from your baseline run.

If formulas show as text: in Google Sheets use File > Import with 'Convert text to numbers, dates, and formulas' on; in Excel locales that use ; as the list separator, import via Data > From Text/CSV with comma as the delimiter.
